rows.label: STRENGTH
rows.description: Turn it down if the wheel is too strong to hold.

rows.label: STEERING WEIGHT
rows.description: Turn it up for a heavier wheel in corners, down for a lighter one.

rows.label: SELF-CENTRING
rows.description: Turn it up to pull the wheel back to the middle harder.

rows.label: DAMPING
rows.description: Turn it up to make the wheel slower and heavier to turn.

rows.label: ROAD EFFECTS
rows.description: Turn it up to feel kerbs, bumps and crashes more.

rows.label: ENGINE VIBRATION
rows.description: Turn it down if the wheel buzzes all the time.

rows.label: CENTRE FEEL
rows.description: Turn it up if the wheel feels loose and empty when you drive straight.

rows.label: SMOOTH JOLTS
rows.description: Turn it up to soften sudden kicks, like gear changes; kerbs stay sharp.

rows.label: STEERING LOCK
rows.description: Turn it down to steer quicker: less turning of your wheel for full lock.

expert.description: Report the wheel as a 900-degree wheel (Gamepad.sThumbLX = 900 in its capabilities), so FH1 uses its linear 900-degree steering instead of the default wheel mapping, which cuts steering at speed. Set the base to 900 degrees. Read when the wheel connects
Brake axis, as wheel_throttle
Brake dead zone at rest, in percent of travel; -1 uses wheel_pedal_deadzone
Brake dead zone at full travel, in percent: past it reads fully pressed

Wheel buttons as pad controls: "NAME=[device|]N" pairs separated by commas, N a button number or hN.up/down/left/right for a hat; names as in pad_remap (A, B, X, Y, LB, RB, LT, RT, LS, RS, BACK, START, UP, ...), or GEAR1 to GEAR7 and REVERSE for an H-shifter's gates
Clutch axis, as wheel_throttle. A wheel's clutch is analog on the right stick's vertical axis, where FH1's wheel layouts read it
Pad button the clutch pedal also presses past half travel; empty for none. In FH1's wheel layout 1 LB shifts down, so leave it empty there
Clutch dead zone at rest, in percent of travel; -1 uses wheel_pedal_deadzone
Clutch dead zone at full travel, in percent: past it reads fully pressed
The wheel base: empty for the first device SDL reports as a wheel, "vvvv:pppp" (USB IDs in hex) or part of its name
Read racing wheels raw, each axis and button bound per device (wheel_*), as one XInput wheel (subtype 2) that plays the title's own force feedback; off uses the SDL gamepad path (hid_wheel_*)
Host centring spring in percent, added to the title's forces
Device that receives force feedback, as wheel_device; empty for the steering device (for EmuWheel/vJoy, the vJoy device relays it)
Play the title's own wheel force feedback effects (XInputdFF: spring, damper, friction, inertia and constant force) on the wheel
Strength in percent of the title's friction effect
Strength in percent of the title's inertia effect
Reverse the force feedback direction
Full-scale value of the title's effect magnitudes and coefficients (DirectInput's 10000); the FFB trace shows the values it sends
Lifts any non-zero steering force to at least this percent, so small forces get past a geared or belted wheel's friction (a direct-drive base needs 0)
Force feedback: difference (the title's two motor values as a signed constant force, right minus left), left-signed or right-signed (one motor alone, 0x8000 = no force), rumble, or off
Strength in percent of the title's wheel rumble (kerbs, impacts), played as a vibration on top of the effects
Full-scale value of the title's effect saturations and dead bands; 0 decides per effect (255 when every value fits a byte, else 10000)
Write the title's force feedback calls (motor values, caller, wheel steering and pedals, host force) to a CSV beside the runtime log
Path of the force feedback trace; empty writes ffb-trace-<time>.csv beside the runtime log
Handbrake axis, as wheel_throttle: analog on the left stick's vertical axis, where FM4's wheel layouts read it
Handbrake dead zone at rest, in percent of travel; -1 uses wheel_pedal_deadzone
Handbrake dead zone at full travel, in percent: past it reads fully pressed
While a racing wheel is connected, hide other SDL gamepads from the title so none of them takes player one
Log wheel axis, button and hat changes and the title's motor values, to find the numbers for the wheel bindings
Pedal deadzone in percent of travel
Steering axis on the wheel base
Steering deadzone in percent of half travel
Reverse the steering axis
Throttle axis: "[device|][+|-]axisN"; device as in wheel_device (empty: the wheel base), + or - forces the pedal direction, which is otherwise detected from its resting value
Throttle dead zone at rest, in percent of travel; -1 uses wheel_pedal_deadzone
Throttle dead zone at full travel, in percent: past it reads fully pressed
